scope: Native State Machine verification in the existing isolated Python project workspace

source_cases.preparation: Reuse complete language-independent state/trigger matrices, structural fact recipes, guard predictions and malformed-input outcomes without dropping cases
source_cases.capacity: Retain existing 4096-case bounds; capacity exhaustion leaves the whole row not_evaluable, never a passing prefix

native_contract.input: Translate shared string-symbol recipes into generated nominal State/Trigger members only at the verifier boundary; public reducers still reject raw strings, role swaps, foreign enums and forged members
native_contract.facts: Use inert Python structural carriers without Entity or Value Object factory validation, retaining exact existing UInt64, set, list, optional and sum behavior
native_contract.outcome: Check exact initial state, transition or rejection, nominal output state, transition identifier, and authored ordered output-intent slots and Event references
native_contract.integrity: Require frozen callable, descriptor, slot-based results, tuple intents and immutable mappings; replay twice with fresh outcomes and no input mutation or coercion
native_contract.effects: Audit bounded native reducer replay; intents remain data and are not constructed, published, persisted or dispatched
native_contract.independent_observation: Reuse whole provider/facade grammar and independent checked-type grammar; bind Event bodies and Rule/runtime dependency bytes; transitive Rules are observed before reducer execution
native_contract.negative_controls: Three callable binding mutations, native nominal rejections and two compiling whole-source substitutions for every selected State Machine

execution: One existing bounded isolated semantic process; no new workspace, external dependency, emitter oracle or runtime mode
claim_ceiling: Bounded source conformance only; not arbitrary Python sandboxing, event execution, external effect authorization, full CLI qualification or release
